whatYouGet: One Tracer LGP01 Blade putter, right hand
clubHeadline: The one for a stroke that already arcs.
clubParas: A blade putter does less for you than a mallet and asks more in return, which is exactly why better putters keep going back to them. There is more feel in a small head and more information in a mishit.

It is cast 431 stainless at 385 grams — heavy for a blade, which is what stops the hands taking over on a short one. Loft is 3.5 degrees, enough to lift the ball out of its own dent and start it rolling early.

35 inches, right hand, with the Lucky rubber grip rather than the oversized 3.0 that ships on the mallet. That is a deliberate pairing: an arcing stroke wants to feel the club, and a fat grip takes that away.
It is $199 because we sell it to you directly — there is more on the pricing if you want it.

clubSpecs.v: Solid and heavy. A blade tells you where you hit it.
Lucky rubber, stock — not the oversized 3.0.

look.photo: Bold, full-bleed, portrait. Blade head at address on the green, low sun along the top line. Shot from the golfer's eyeline so the small head reads as small — that is the appeal.
look.headline: Less club, more information
paras: A blade is the smallest thing you will look down at all round, and every miss tells you about itself. That is either the reason to play one or the reason not to.
In gold, at 385 grams, it is also the least apologetic putter we make.
look.aside: Everyone else is carrying the same putter with someone else's name on it. It's better to be lucky.

closeBody: The Blade is $199, right hand, and sold out at the moment. Sixty days to send it back when it returns.

helpPick.headline: Two putters, and the honest answer is your stroke picks
helpPick.sub: Watch your stroke from behind. If the head arcs inside on the way back and closes through the ball, you want this one. If it travels straight back and straight through, the mallet is the easier club.

options.name: Tracer Blade
options.body: Classic blade that wants to rotate through the ball the way an arcing stroke already does. More feel, less forgiveness, and the one better putters tend to reach for.

options.name: Tracer Mallet
options.body: Wide, face-balanced head that resists twisting and sits square without being aimed. The forgiving one, and it comes in left hand as well.

helpPick.note: The blade is out of stock at the moment and right hand only when it returns. If your stroke wants a blade, that is worth waiting for rather than talking yourself into the other one.
